newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $68-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market slow at $68-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $68.00 per cwt in light volume near midday Wednesday, steady with Tuesday's brisk activity, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head of slaughter steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas. The sales brought week-to-date sales there near 62,000 head, they said.
An estimated 7,000 sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, bringing the weekly movement to about 84,800. The Panhandle-area showlist was said to be almost depleted.
Estimates earlier in the week pegged showlists in the Panhandle near 99,000 head and about 88,000 in Kansas.
Fed cattle prices were seen holding near $68.00 amid strong beef demand from retailers booking orders for seasonal promotions, market sources said.
"The fact that kills have been very good and boxed beef prices have held are very good signs on demand," one source said.

Slaughter through Tuesday was estimated at 264,000 head, compared with 255,000 last week and 265,000 a year ago, USDA reported. Beef sales the first two days this week were pegged at 442 fabricated loads, up 3.4 percent from 330 the same time a week ago, USDA statistics showed.

Sources noted that the upcoming U.S. Memorial Day holiday in late May and Fathers Day in June were considered good demand times for beef consumption, particularly of cuts that lend themselves to outdoor grilling.
